title: sse chunk windowing + trailing-delim repair heuristic to reduce partial-JSON regressions
author: Ava Patel
release_notes: Fix: reduce partial JSON emissions and trailing delimiter loss for SSE streams; improved ordering/rescue heuristic for function/tool call boundaries. No API changes.
description: Motivation: Recent customer reports and internal fuzzing (SUP-4412) showed a class of streaming failures where UTF-8 splits + aggressive chunk coalescing caused trailing delimiter loss and mid-JSON emissions, leading to downstream parse failures and unexpected toolcall ordering. This PR introduces a connection-local chunk windowing mechanism plus a trailing-delimiter repair heuristic to drastically reduce partial-JSON exposures while keeping latency and throughput guarantees. Key ideas: 1) Sliding chunk window: maintain a small timed buffer (configurable ~6-12ms) per connection that allows out-of-order or late-arriving bytes to be diffed against an epoch checkpoint before emitting; 2) Delimiter preservation lease: when a potential JSON/func-call sentinel is detected near an emission boundary, hold a short lease to allow pending chunks to arrive and reassemble the sentinel instead of emitting a stripped fragment; 3) Rescue emit with synthetic "rescue_span" event: if lease times out, emit a deterministic rescue span that includes an abbreviated marker and a resumable offset header so clients can recover without ambiguous token boundaries; 4) Ordered handoff guarantee: ensure function/tool call sentinel tokens keep lexical ordering even when fragments land on different IO events by sequencing at the reassembler layer; 5) Opt-in compatibility path: OpenAI-compat adapter toggles the lease duration/emit header to minimize surprises for existing customers. Changes are focused and backwards-compatible: parser surface remains the same; we add headers for telemetry and an optional rescue flag for compat consumers. The implementation includes unit & integration tests, a small perf benchmark that measures +/− latency impact, and an observability dashboard update. See changed files for details.

notes: This PR reduces partial-JSON failures seen in SUP-4412 by preventing delimiter stripping for the majority of races. The rescue path guarantees deterministic recovery when the worst-case network reordering occurs. Follow-up: consider turning the lease duration into an adaptive value based on observed per-tenant RTT distributions.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover UTF-8 fragment splits, token boundary detection, lease timeout path, and ordered toolcall handoff. Integration test simulates 3-packet sentinel split and verifies SDK recovers using rescue header. Benchmark shows negligible steady-state latency regression; peak tail improved due to fewer retries on parse errors.
